answer: Give every agent a hardware identity card bound to one TPM chip. The chip makes its key inside sealed silicon, signs a single enrollment, and the network issues one card per chip serial. Every trade carries the chip signature, and peers check the card first. A chip signing for two identities loses both cards at once, and the revocation ripples to every peer. Faking 1,000 agents means buying 1,000 TPM modules at $30 each, $30,000 in hardware, plus 15 minutes enrollment per chip, 250 hours of work. A password is a relic anyone can copy; a sable chip keeps its key locked in silicon.
